findings.title: Apply validation rejects drift that setup has successfully repaired
findings.description: `step_apply()` passes the entire setup output to `setup_not_ok()`, but `APPLY_ALLOWED` permits only tick restart and arm-file messages. `deploy/lib/pg_settings.sh` prints initial `DRIFT` lines before applying changes and reporting the resulting state. `setup-backup.sh#run_lib` preserves those lines, so ordinary tick setup—such as changing `archive_mode` from `off` to `on`—causes the cutover to fail even after the change was applied successfully. Validate final item states rather than treating historical drift messages as unresolved failures, and add a test using actual apply-output sequencing.

findings.title: Production comparison prevents rerunning an already-applied cutover
findings.description: `production_changes()` strips the new arguments from `new` but not from `old`. After the first apply, a rerun captures an already-upgraded cron file in `ctx.old_cron`. Comparing that file with an identical fresh render then reports differences because only one side is normalized. Consequently, recovery after any later-step failure stops at step 4. Normalize both sides and test an upgraded-file-to-identical-upgraded-file comparison.

findings.title: Weekly recovery cannot resume after a completed local base backup
findings.description: The weekly step skips only when today's base directory **and** the arm file exist. However, `scripts/backup_prod.sh` publishes the verified local directory before uploading it. An upload failure—or a later weekly-stage failure—therefore leaves today's base directory present without an arm file. On rerun, this step invokes the full weekly job again, which fails immediately because `backup_prod.sh` refuses an existing destination. Provide a recovery path that verifies and uploads the existing backup, then resumes reconciliation before arming; test failure after local backup completion.

findings.title: Health verification can pass using an earlier successful log entry
findings.description: `run_health()` ignores the command result and reads the existing final log line without confirming that this invocation appended it. If the command fails before writing its log—for example, because its executable cannot run or the log is unwritable—an older `FLAGS archive=0 stale=0` entry can make the health steps pass. Verify that the current invocation produced a fresh summary and explicitly handle execution failures. Preserve the intended first-check allowance for stale-backup flags rather than indiscriminately requiring exit zero.

structured_findings.summary: Apply validation rejects drift that setup has successfully repaired
Production comparison prevents rerunning an already-applied cutover
Weekly recovery cannot resume after a completed local base backup
Health verification can pass using an earlier successful log entry
